I couldn't write these notes. The first batch of page fetches crashed because of a bug in my script, before any page content was saved. When I tried again, the research tool said I had no calls left for this turn. So I haven't read any pages, and I can't get to the web another way.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have nothing from the sources, any verse notes I wrote now would break those rules, so I've left them all out.

**What I planned to read when you ask me to continue:**
- **Verse-by-verse traditional reading:** enduringword.com (Guzik on Lamentations 1); preceptaustin.org's Lamentations 1 commentary; and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com for Lamentations 1.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** searches on ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, spurgeon.org, wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), seedbed.com, enduringword.com, ag.org, lcms.org and 1517.org. I'd especially look at verses 12, 18 and 21–22, where readings tend to differ.
- **Other views:**
  - Modern scholarship: bibleodyssey.org on Lamentations and Daughter Zion, and the netbible.org notes.
  - Catholic and Orthodox: newadvent.org (the Catholic Encyclopedia article on Lamentations and the Church Fathers), catholic.com and oca.org, including how Lamentations is used in Holy Week services.
  - Popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace), only if these sites discuss it in connection with this chapter.

If you start a new turn, I'll fetch these pages and write the notes verse by verse ("v. 1: …"), with a URL after every point and anything I can't find left out.
